tldr: For arbitrary bounded affine responses in disjoint fixed experimental blocks, the public-threshold endpoint-shortfall contrast has unrestricted original-record minimax squared risk \(R_{\mathrm{SL}}(b,d)\asymp\psi(b,d)\) for every integer \(d\ge1\) and \(1\le b\le2^{d/2}\). A total estimator with rational public branch selection attains the upper bound. Explicit supported moment-matched priors, global weak-derivative smoothing, a full labeled numerical-record comparison including the all-control atom, and a realized-target variance charge prove the matching converse. The order comparison and every finite sample branch are discharged. By parameter-set inclusion, the converse also holds for every containing bounded response class under this same experiment, target and estimator class; the affine upper bound does not transfer. The result provides a prospective precision benchmark for the fixed-threshold shortfall component of the RUMI downside workflow. The unrestricted critical and larger-sample matched-risk transition remains outside the headline.
